title: Lack of Forwarding/Deprecation Layers (Breaking Upgrades)
pattern: Directly modifying or deleting a public type, method, or parameter in a minor or patch upgrade, rather than providing an incremental transition path.
why_bad: It breaks downstream consumer builds instantly upon upgrade, preventing incremental adoption and creating a cascade of compile failures. It forces consumers to halt feature work to fix breaking dependencies.
detection: Modifying the signature of any public symbol without marking the old symbol as `#[deprecated]` or providing a forwarding function.
counterexample: Major version upgrades (breaking changes) where breaking backward compatibility is expected and documented.
fix: Provide a deprecation layer. Keep the old method signature, mark it with `#[deprecated]`, and have its body calculate the default and delegate to the new method.
source: Jon Gjengset, *Rust for Rustaceans* (2021), Chapter 4 ("Type Modifications"), pp. 91-94; Titus Winters et al., *Software Engineering at Google* (2020), Chapter 22 ("Language Support").
